title: Choose the safe table operation
prompt: You need one row per customer before joining to a customer-level target. What should you verify first?
explanation: Grain and key uniqueness determine whether the join duplicates observations.

title: Choose the SQL operation
prompt: You need revenue by region after filtering cancelled orders. Which order is logically safest?
explanation: Filter invalid rows before aggregation so grouped values describe the intended population.

title: Choose the spreadsheet tool
prompt: You need a reusable import-clean-refresh workflow from a CSV. Which tool fits best?
explanation: Power Query records transformation steps and supports refresh.

title: Choose an imputation strategy
prompt: Income is skewed with strong outliers and 8% values missing. Which simple baseline is usually safer than mean imputation?
explanation: Median is less sensitive to extreme values, though the missingness mechanism still matters.

title: Spot the preprocessing rule
prompt: Which workflow avoids scaling leakage?
options: Fit scaler on training rows and transform validation/test
Fit separate scalers on train and test
explanation: Preprocessing parameters must be learned from training evidence only.

title: Choose an encoding
prompt: A nominal colour feature has values red, blue and green with no natural order. Which default encoding is safer than integer 1/2/3?
explanation: One-hot encoding avoids introducing an artificial numeric ordering for nominal categories.

title: Interpret EDA carefully
prompt: Two variables have strong correlation. Which conclusion is safest?
options: They move together in this sample; causality needs stronger design/evidence
explanation: EDA reveals patterns and hypotheses, not automatic causal identification.

title: Choose an honest visual
prompt: Which change is most likely to mislead viewers about the magnitude of a small difference?
options: Truncating the bar-chart axis far above zero without clear justification
explanation: For magnitude comparisons, a severely truncated bar baseline can exaggerate differences.

title: Protect the final test set
prompt: What is the role of the final test set?
options: A final independent estimate after model-development choices are complete
explanation: The test set should represent independent final evidence, not a development feedback loop.

title: Choose the right CV
prompt: Three recordings belong to each participant. Which CV method best prevents participant leakage?
options: Leave the same participant in train and validation
explanation: Group-aware validation keeps all observations from one entity on the same side of a fold.

title: Spot leakage
prompt: Which preprocessing workflow leaks validation information?
options: Fit imputer inside each training fold
Fit scaler on the entire dataset before cross-validation
explanation: Fitting preprocessing before the split allows held-out rows to influence learned transformation parameters.

title: Diagnose linear regression
prompt: Residuals show a strong U-shaped pattern against fitted values. What does this suggest?
options: The linear form is missing nonlinearity
explanation: Systematic residual shape indicates that the linear mean function is not capturing the relationship.

title: Interpret logistic regression
prompt: What does logistic regression model linearly before the sigmoid transformation?
options: The log-odds of the positive class
explanation: The linear predictor is mapped to probability through the logistic link.

title: Control tree complexity
prompt: Validation error rises while training error keeps falling as depth increases. What should you do first?
options: Use the test set to choose depth
explanation: The pattern is consistent with overfitting.

title: Reason about an ensemble
prompt: Why does a Random Forest randomise both rows and candidate features?
options: To decorrelate tree errors before averaging
explanation: Diversity among competent trees makes averaging more effective.

title: Reason about boosting
prompt: What does a new boosting learner usually focus on?
explanation: Boosting adds learners that correct errors left by the current ensemble.

title: Choose k
prompt: What is the usual effect of increasing k in KNN?
explanation: Larger neighbourhoods reduce local variance but can increase bias.

title: Interpret C
prompt: Increasing C in a soft-margin SVM generally makes violations…
explanation: Higher C penalises margin violations more strongly.

title: Choose k responsibly
prompt: Which approach is better than selecting k only by eye?
options: Combine domain meaning with diagnostics such as silhouette
Use the test labels during clustering
explanation: Cluster count should combine structure diagnostics and domain interpretability.

title: Reason about PCA
prompt: What does the first principal component maximise?
options: Variance of projected data subject to the component constraints
explanation: PCA finds orthogonal directions that capture as much variance as possible; it does not use class labels.

title: Choose the decision policy
prompt: A screening system must miss as few positive cases as possible. Which metric deserves special attention?
explanation: Recall measures the fraction of actual positives detected.

title: Read the residual signal
prompt: Residual spread increases as predictions increase. What pattern is this?
explanation: Changing residual variance suggests heteroscedasticity and may affect uncertainty/metric interpretation.

title: Diagnose high variance
prompt: Training error is very low but validation error is much higher. Which diagnosis is most plausible?
explanation: A large train–validation gap is a classic high-variance signal.

title: Reason about regularisation
prompt: What is the usual purpose of increasing regularisation strength?
options: Discourage overly complex parameter values to improve generalisation
Use the test set more often
explanation: Regularisation trades some training fit for simpler parameter values and often lower variance.

title: Protect evaluation
prompt: Where should hyperparameter search occur?
options: Inside training/validation workflow, keeping final test untouched
On the final test set repeatedly
explanation: The final test set should remain independent of model selection.

title: Read calibration
prompt: Among cases predicted near 0.8 probability, only about 0.5 are positive. The model is…
options: Over-confident / poorly calibrated in that region
explanation: Calibration compares predicted probability with observed frequency.

title: Interpret an explanation
prompt: A SHAP or permutation-importance result shows a feature matters to predictions. What can you safely conclude?
options: The model relies on that feature under the explanation assumptions
The feature should always be removed
explanation: Model explanations describe predictive behaviour, not causal truth.

title: Interpret prediction intervals
prompt: A nominal 90% prediction interval is well calibrated when, over comparable future cases…
options: About 90% of outcomes fall inside the intervals
The point prediction is always exact
explanation: Coverage is a repeated-sample property: interval calibration concerns how often future outcomes are contained.

title: Protect time order
prompt: Which validation approach is safest for a forecasting model?
explanation: Forecast validation must preserve chronology so future information does not leak backward.

title: Tune learning rate
prompt: If loss oscillates or explodes immediately, which parameter is a prime suspect?
explanation: Oversized updates can overshoot useful regions of the loss surface.

title: Interpret attention
prompt: What is safest to say about a high attention weight?
options: It indicates stronger weighting in that attention computation
explanation: Attention weights describe weighting, not necessarily causal explanation.

title: Reason about message passing
prompt: After two GNN layers, a node can usually incorporate information from…
explanation: Each message-passing layer expands the receptive field by about one hop.

title: Diagnose drift
prompt: Feature distributions change but P(y|x) appears stable. What kind of shift is this closest to?
explanation: Input distributions can drift without the predictive relationship changing. Concept drift specifically changes the relationship between inputs and outcome.
